🚀 Key Quantum Sensing Startups (Active Today)
Atom-Interferometry & Navigation Sensors

AOSense / AOSense Defense – U.S. company building cold-atom inertial sensors (gravimeters, rotation sensors) for GPS-denied navigation and defense applications.

Aquark Technologies – UK spin-out developing portable quantum navigation and timing sensors, tested at sea in collaboration with the Royal Navy. 
quantum.org.uk

Delta g – UK startup using cold atom gravimetry for geophysical and infrastructure sensing markets. 
quantum.org.uk

Mesa Quantum – U.S. startup building chip-scale quantum sensors for inertial navigation and magnetometry, supported by Space Force grants.

Diamond & Spin-Based Quantum Magnetometry

Qnami AG – Swiss company commercializing diamond NV-center quantum microscopes for ultra-precise magnetic field imaging in materials science and semiconductors.

KWAN-TEK – French firm leveraging diamond quantum sensors for precision metrology applications.

IonQ (via Vector Atomic) – After acquiring Vector Atomic, IonQ now includes advanced atomic clocks, sensors, and PNT (positioning/navigation/timing) tech in its offering.

🧭 Technology Areas Covered

Quantum sensing startups today are applying diverse physics platforms, including:
✔ Cold atoms / atom interferometry for inertial navigation and gravimetry
✔ Diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers for magnetic imaging and magnetometry
✔ Chip-scale atomic/photonics sensors for miniaturized field detection
✔ Nanodiamond biomedical sensors for single-cell diagnostics
✔ Quantum dots / SWIR imaging for enhanced medical imaging and industrial inspection

📈 Market & Trends

Quantum sensing is increasingly commercializing beyond labs into defense, aerospace, healthcare, semiconductors, and natural-resources markets.

Defence and navigation (GPS-denied positioning) are major early adopters, driving funding and contracts.

Biomedical sensing (e.g., single-cell diagnostics) and semiconductor diagnostics are emerging high-growth niches.

Venture funding, grants, and government partnerships continue to accelerate startups from spin-outs to early commercial deployments.
